reason: I've got free YouTube sleep stuff and my sleep score already tells me how I did. A meditation a machine wrote about my feelings in a minute just sounds a bit off to me.
objection: AI-made meditation is going to sound generic, or weirdly personal in a creepy way.
would_change_my_mind: A friend sending me a session it made that actually sounded human, so I could hear it without signing up.

v1.why: Opens on someone else's chat and a coin counter; feels like a game, not something for me.

v2.why: Cleaner, but still percentages that are clearly made up.

v3.why: The Why? on changes helps the creepy feeling, but I still would not swap my free stuff.

reason: I'd try it the day I heard about it, and if the first couple of sessions really sound made for me I'd pay for a month to get the longer ones and the other voices. Whether I'm still paying in month three is another question.
objection: It becomes one more subscription I stop opening after two weeks.

v1.why: The example conversation that isn't mine and a menu to dig through; I'd lose interest.

v2.why: Chapter 2 being ready tomorrow gives me a reason to come back.

v3.why: Progress in words and a report every two weeks is the bit I'd actually tell friends about.

reason: Free, a few a day? Sure, I'll try it, the Hard to sleep chip means I don't have to write an essay. But $10 a month is a bill I don't have room for when YouTube is free.
objection: When I feel bad I don't want to type out how I feel, and I'm not paying for something I might use twice.
would_change_my_mind: A much cheaper plan, like $3 a month, or the free tier being enough that I never need to think about it.

v1.why: Daily check-in with notes is exactly the typing I don't want.

v2.why: Three skippable questions are fine, but I'd drift back to YouTube.

v3.why: A journal I don't have to keep and progress in plain words; I'd keep it on the free tier.

reason: I don't want an AI writing scripts about my mental state, and I don't have a spare evening to test whether it's safe. The kids, work, and I'd forget it anyway.
objection: Who checked what the AI says to someone who is actually struggling, and will I even remember to open it?
would_change_my_mind: Seeing that a real clinician or meditation teacher reviews what it generates.

v1.why: Percentages and arrows about my wellness from an AI feel like nonsense dressed up as data.

v2.why: Nicer start, but the same AI underneath.

v3.why: The Why? and no rankings are the right instincts; still not enough for me to trust it.

reason: Forty minutes on the train each way is a perfect slot to try it. But I'd want to see my Oura numbers move before paying, and right now the wearable readings are only examples.
objection: Is this actually helping or just a nice sound bath with an AI label on it?
would_change_my_mind: A real link to my ring that shows my HRV or sleep after sessions versus without, over a few weeks.

v1.why: The numbers are obviously sample data and the menu is fiddly on the train.

v2.why: Tabs, a journey, and at least it tries to put numbers on progress.

v3.why: Asking for my wearable is right, but progress in words instead of numbers is the opposite of what I want.

reason: My one free hour after the kids are down is for me, and I already have free stuff. I'm not telling an app how I'm doing mentally without knowing where that goes.
objection: What happens to what I tell it about my mental state, and who gets to see it?
would_change_my_mind: A plain, short promise that what I type isn't stored or sold, and a way to try it without an account.

v1.why: Check-ins and notes every day, with nothing saying where they go.

v2.why: Asks how I feel right away; still no word on privacy.

v3.why: Private journal and wearable off by default are good signs, but I'd need it spelled out.

reason: I'd try it on the commute, since I use apps between therapy sessions anyway. I'll only pay once I know it doesn't sound like a generic AI reading a mindfulness template back at me.
objection: AI-made meditation probably sounds generic, and the stuff I'd tell it is sensitive.
would_change_my_mind: Three or four sessions in a row that clearly picked up on what I said, in a voice I actually like.

v1.why: Scoring my wellness in percentages is something my therapist would never do.

v2.why: Asking 'How do you feel now?' after a session is the right question.

v3.why: Words not scores, a private journal and a Why? feel like they were designed by someone who gets it.

reason: I'd try it at bedtime because I'm in bed with my phone anyway. But my sleep sounds on YouTube are free and work fine; a few free sessions a day is more than I'd need.
objection: I already have free apps and YouTube for this.
would_change_my_mind: Sleep stories that are clearly better than what I get free, plus a cheaper plan.

v1.why: Too much going on when I just want to press play and sleep.

v2.why: Tell it I can't sleep, press play, done; I'd use the free tier.

v3.why: Fine too, but journals and reports are stuff I'd ignore at bedtime.

reason: I paid for Calm once and stopped after a month, so I know how this goes. I'd try the free bit, but I'm not paying again until I see I'm still opening it after a few weeks.
objection: Will it actually help, or is it a gimmick that I'll drop like the last one?
would_change_my_mind: Still using it on the free tier after three or four weeks; then maybe I'd pay.

v1.why: Feels like Calm with coins; I'd drop it the same way.

v2.why: The chapter tomorrow is a nice hook but I know I'd miss days.

v3.why: Best of the three, but I'd likely drift off by week three like before.

reason: I'm awake scrolling anyway, so typing 'my mind won't stop' into this instead is easy to try. But I've never paid for one of these and free YouTube gets me through; a few free sessions is plenty.
objection: Will it actually help me sleep, or just be something else to scroll through at midnight?
would_change_my_mind: If it actually got me to sleep faster most nights for a couple of weeks, I'd think about the annual plan.

v1.why: A daily check-in form at 1am is the last thing I want.

v2.why: Short questions, then a session from my own words; I'd use it on bad nights.

v3.why: Same, and hearing in words whether I'm sleeping better would keep me coming back.
